speaker: Sheldon
text: You know, I've been thinking about time travel again.

speaker: Leonard
text: Why? Did you hit a roadblock with invisibility?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Put it on the back burner. Anyway, it occurs to me, if I ever did perfect a time machine... I'd go into the past and give it to myself. Thus eliminating the need for me to invent it in the first place. - Interesting. - Yeah, it really takes the pressure off.

speaker: Leonard
text: Sounds like a breakthrough. Should I call science and tell them to hold the cover?

speaker: Sheldon
text: It's time travel, Leonard. I will have done that.

speaker: Leonard
text: I guess congratulations are in order.

speaker: Sheldon
text: No, congratulations will have been in order. You know, I'm not going to enjoy this party.

speaker: Leonard
text: I know, I'm familiar with you.

speaker: Sheldon
text: The last party, professor finkleday cornered me... And talked about spelunking for 45 minutes.

speaker: Leonard
text: Yes, I was there.

speaker: Sheldon
text: You know what's interesting aboutcaves?

speaker: Leonard
text: - What? - Nothing. We'll avoid finkleday, meet the new head, congratulate him, shake his hand and go.

speaker: Sheldon
text: How's this? "Pleased to meet you, Dr. Gablehauser. How fortunate for you the university has chosen to hire you... Despite the fact you've done no original research in 25 years... And instead have written books... That reduce the great concepts of science to anecdotes... Each one dumbed down... To accommodate the duration of an average bowel movement."

speaker: Leonard
text: - "Mahalo" is a nice touch. - Hmm.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Only eight consonants in the Hawaiian language.

speaker: Leonard
text: Interesting, you should lead with that.

speaker: Raj
text: Oh, god, look at this buffet. I love america. - You don't have buffets in India? - Of course, but it's all Indian food. You can't find a bagel in Mumbai to save your life. Smear me.

speaker: Sheldon
text: - Well, here's an interesting turn of events. - What?

speaker: Leonard
text: Howard brought a date?

speaker: Sheldon
text: A more plausible explanation is that his work in robotics has made an amazing leap.

speaker: Howard
text: Hey, what up, science bitches? May I introduce my special lady friend, summer.

speaker: Summer
text: Howard, I told you, touching's extra.

speaker: Howard
text: Right. Sorry.

speaker: unknown
text: Here comes our new boss. Be polite.

speaker: Gablehouser
text: Hi, fellas.

speaker: Howard
text: - Eric gablehauser. - Howard Wolowitz.

speaker: Gablehouser
text: Howard, nice to meet you. And you are?

speaker: Sheldon
text: An actual real scientist.

speaker: Sheldon
text: How was that? I can't believe he fired me.

speaker: Leonard
text: You did call him a glorified science teacher... Whose last successful experiment was lighting his own farts.

speaker: Sheldon
text: In my defense, I prefaced that by saying "with all due respect."

speaker: Leonard
text: Morning.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Morning.

speaker: Leonard
text: You're making eggs for breakfast?

speaker: Sheldon
text: This isn't breakfast, it's an experiment.

speaker: Leonard
text: Oh. Because it looks a lot like breakfast.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I finally have time to test my hypothesis about the separation of water molecules... From the egg proteins and its impact vis-a-vis taste.

speaker: Leonard
text: Sounds yummy. I look fonnard to your work with bacon.

speaker: Leonard
text: You know, I'm sure if you just apologize to gablehauser he'd give your job back.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I don't want my job back. I've spent three and a half years staring at grease boards full of equations. Before that, I spent four years working on my thesis. Before that, I was in college, and before that I was in the fifth grade. This is my first day off in decades and I'm going to savor it.

speaker: Leonard
text: Okay. I'll let you get back to fixing your eggs.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I'm not just fixing my eggs, I'm fixing everyone's eggs.

speaker: Leonard
text: And we all thank you.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Use new eggs.

speaker: unknown
text: Hi, I'm running out to the market. Do you guys need anything?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Oh. This would be one of those circumstances... People unfamiliar with the law of large numbers would call a coincidence.

speaker: Penny
text: - I'm sorry? - I need eggs.

speaker: Sheldon
text: - Four dozen should suffice. - Fourdozen? Evenly distributed amongst brown, white, free-range, large, extra-large and jumbo. - Okay, one more time? - Never mind, you won't get it right. I'd better come with you.

speaker: Penny
text: Oh, yay.

speaker: Penny
text: How come you didn't go in to work today?

speaker: Sheldon
text: I'm taking a sabbatical because I won't kowtow to mediocre minds.

speaker: Penny
text: So you got canned, huh?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Theoretical physicists do not get canned. But, yeah.

speaker: Penny
text: Maybe it's for the best. You know, I always say, "when one door closes, another one opens."

speaker: Sheldon
text: No, it doesn't. Not unless the doors are connected by relays. - Or there are motion sensors involved. - No, I meant... Or if the first door closing creates a change of air pressure that acts upon the second.

speaker: Penny
text: Never mind.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Slow down. Slow down. Please, slow down.

speaker: Penny
text: We're fine.

speaker: Sheldon
text: You're not leaving enough space between cars.

speaker: Penny
text: Oh, sure I am.

speaker: Sheldon
text: No, no, let me do the math for you. This car weighs, let's say, 4000 pounds. Now, add 140 for me, 120 for you... - One-twenty? - Oh, I'm sorry, did I insult you? Is your body mass somehow tied into your self-worth?

speaker: Penny
text: Well, yeah.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Interesting. Anyway, that gives us a total weight of, let's say, 4400 pounds.

speaker: Penny
text: Let's say 4390.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Fine. We're traveling fonnard at... Good lord... 51 miles an hour. Let's assume that your brakes are new and the calipers are aligned. By the time we come to a stop... We'll be occupying the same space as that buick. An impossibility that nature will quickly resolve into death, mutilation and... Oh, look, they built a new putt-putt course.

speaker: Sheldon
text: This is great. Look at me. I'm in the real world of ordinary people... Just living their ordinary, colorless, work-a-day lives. - Thank you. - No, thank you. And thank you, ordinary person. Hey, you wanna hear an interesting thing about tomatoes?

speaker: Penny
text: No. No, not really. Listen, didn't you say you needed some eggs?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Yes, but anyone who knows anything about bacterial growth... Knows to pick up their refrigerated foods on the way out.

speaker: Penny
text: Oh, okay, maybe you should start heading on out, then.

speaker: Sheldon
text: No, this is fun. The thing about tomatoes, and I think you'll enjoy this... Is they're shelved with the vegetables, but they're technically a fruit. - Hmm. Interesting. - Isn't it?

speaker: Penny
text: No, I mean what you find enjoyable.

speaker: unknown
text: Oh, boy.

speaker: Penny
text: What now?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Well, there's some value to taking a multivitamin... But the human body can only absorb so much. What you're buying here are the ingredients for very expensive urine.

speaker: Penny
text: Well, maybe that's what I was going for.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Well, then you'll want some manganese.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Well, that was fun. Tomorrow we can go to one of those warehouse stores.

speaker: Penny
text: I don't know, Sheldon. It's gonna take me a while to recover from all the fun I had today.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Are you sure? There are a lot of advantages to buying in bulk. For example, I noticed you purchase your tampons... One month's supply at a time.

speaker: Sheldon
text: - What? - Well, think about it. It doesn't spoil... And you're going to be needing them for at least the next 30 years.

speaker: Penny
text: You want me to buy 30 years' worth of tampons?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Well, 30, 35... - When did your mother go into menopause? - Okay.

speaker: Penny
text: I'm not talking about this with you.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Oh, penny. This is a natural human process and we're talking about significant savings. Now, if you assume 15 tampons per cycle in a 28-day cycle... Are you fairly regular?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Okay, no warehouse store, but we're still on for putt-putt golf, right?

speaker: unknown
text: Hey, I just ran into penny. She seemed upset about something.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I think it's her time of the month.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I marked the calendar for future reference.

speaker: Leonard
text: What's with the fish?

speaker: Sheldon
text: It's an experiment.

speaker: Leonard
text: - What happened to your egg research? - Oh, that was a dead end.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Scrambled eggs are as good as they're ever going to be.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I read an article about scientists who inserted DNA from luminous jellyfish... Into other animals, and I thought, "hey, fish nightlights."

speaker: Leonard
text: Fish nightlights.

speaker: Sheldon
text: It's a billion-dollar idea. Shhh!

speaker: Leonard
text: Mum's the word.

speaker: Leonard
text: Are you sure you don't wanna just apologize to gablehauser and get your job back?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Oh, no, no, no. No, I have too much to do.

speaker: Leonard
text: Like luminous fish. - Shhh! - I'm sorry, I didn't...

speaker: Sheldon
text: That's just the beginning. I also have an idea for a bulk, mail-order feminine hygiene company. Oh, glow-in-the-dark tampons.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Leonard, we're gonna be rich.

speaker: Leonard
text: - Thanks for coming on such short notice. - You did the right thing calling. I didn't know what to do. He's lost all focus. Every day, he's got a new obsession.

speaker: Leonard
text: This is a particularly disturbing one.

speaker: unknown
text: Mommy?

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: Hi, baby.

speaker: unknown
text: You called my mother?

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: Oh, you got yourself a loom. How nice. - Thank you. - Honey, why did you get a loom?

speaker: Sheldon
text: I was working with luminous fish and I thought, "hey... Loom."

speaker: Sheldon
text: Mom, what are you doing here?

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: Leonard called me.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I know, but why?

speaker: Leonard
text: Because one of the great minds of the 21st century... Is raising glow-in-the-dark fish and weaving serapes.

speaker: Sheldon
text: This is not a serape. This is a poncho. A serape is open at the sides, a poncho is closed. This is a poncho. And neither is a reason to call someone's mother.

speaker: Leonard
text: Really? When was the last time you left the house?

speaker: Sheldon
text: I went to the market with penny.

speaker: Leonard
text: Yeah, that was three weeks ago.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Well, then, buckle up. In the next four to eight days, she's going to get very crabby.

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: Sweetheart, your little friend is concerned about you.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Yes, well, I'm not a child. I'm a grown man capable of living my life as I see fit. And I certainly don't need someone telling on me to my mother.

speaker: Leonard
text: Wait, where are you going?

speaker: Sheldon
text: To my room and no one's allowed in.

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: - He gets his temper from his daddy. - Ah. - He's got my eyes. - I see. All that science stuff, that comes from Jesus.

speaker: Leonard
text: Sheldon, your mom made dinner.

speaker: unknown
text: I'm not hungry.

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: Oh. Leonard, don't trouble yourself. He's stubborn. He may stay in there till the rapture.

speaker: Penny
text: Are we so sure that's a bad thing?

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: I love the boy to death... But he has been difficult since he fell out of me at the kmart.

speaker: Howard
text: Excuse me for being so bold... But I now see where Sheldon gets his smoldering good looks.

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: Oh. Honey, that ain't gonna work, but you keep trying. I made chicken. I hope that isn't one of the animals that you people think is magic.

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: You know, we have an Indian gentleman at our church. A Dr. Patel. It's a beautiful story. The lord spoke to him and moved him to give us all 20 percent off on lasek. You know, those that needed it.

speaker: Leonard
text: That is a lovely story. Are we gonna do anything about Sheldon?

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: Oh, we will. You have to take your time with Sheldon. His father, god rest his soul, used to say: "Mary, you have to take your time with Sheldon."

speaker: Leonard
text: - Sounds like a wise man. - Oh, not so wise.

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: He once tried to fight a bobcat for some licorice. So everybody grab a plate and a pretty placemat that Shelly wove.

speaker: Penny
text: Has Shelly ever freaked out like this before?

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: Oh, all the time. I remember one summer when he was 13... He built a small nuclear reactor in the shed... And told everybody he was gonna provide electricity for the town. Well, the only problem was, he had no, what you call, fissionable materials. Anyway, when he went on the Internet to get some... A man from the government came by and sat him down real gentle... And told him it's against the law to have yellow cake uranium in a shed. - Well, what happened? - Well, poor boy had a fit. Locked himself in his room and built a Sonic death ray. - A death ray? - Well, that's what he called it. Didn't even slow down the neighbor kids. Heh.

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: It pissed our dog off to no end.

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: You know, you two make a cute couple.

speaker: Leonard
text: I... no, no. No, we're not a couple. We're singles. Two singles. Like those individually wrapped slices of cheese that...

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: - Did I pluck a nerve there? - Oh, yeah. Okay. All right, everybody, it's time to eat. Oh, lord, we thank you for this meal and for all your bounty. And we pray that you help Sheldon get back on his rocker. Now, after a moment of silent meditation, I'm gonna end with "in Jesus' name"... But you two don't feel any obligation to join in.

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: Unless, of course, the holy spirit moves you.

speaker: Penny
text: Oh, my god, this is the best cobbler I've ever had.

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: It was always Sheldon's favorite. You know what the secret ingredient is?

speaker: Howard
text: - Hey, look who's com... - Shh. You'll spook him.

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: He's like a baby deer. You gotta let him come to you.

speaker: Leonard
text: This is ridiculous. Damn it, Sheldon, snap out of it. You're a physicist. You belong at the university doing research, not in your room.

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: You don't hunt, do you?

speaker: unknown
text: Good morning, snickerdoodle.

speaker: Sheldon
text: - Morning. - Oh.

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: Well, that looks awful fancy. What is that?

speaker: Sheldon
text: It's my idea of what DNA would look like in a silicon-based life form.

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: But intelligently designed by a creator, right?

speaker: Sheldon
text: What do you want, mom?

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: You know how your daddy used to say that you can only fish for so long... Before you gotta throw a stick of dynamite in the water? - Yeah? - Well, I'm done fishing.

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: - You put those on. - What for? Because you're gonna go to your office... Apologize to your boss and get your job back. - No. - I'm sorry. Did I start that sentence with the words "if it please your highness"?

speaker: Sheldon
text: I'm not going to. I didn't say anything that wasn't true.

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: Now, you listen here. I have been telling you since you were 4. It's okay to be smarter than everybody, but you can't go around pointing it out. - Why not? - Because people don't like it.

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: Remember all the ass-kickings from the neighbor kids?

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: Now, let's get cracking. Shower, shirt, shoes and let's shove off.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Wouldn't have been any ass-kickings if that stupid death ray had worked.

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: Problem solved.

speaker: Leonard
text: Really? That's impressive.

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: Leonard, the lord never gives us more than we can handle. Thankfully, he blessed me with two other children... Who are dumb as soup.

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: Excuse me, Dr. Gablehauser, are you busy? - Well, actually... - Sheldon, he's just doodling. Get in here.

speaker: Gablehouser
text: - Dr. Gablehauser. - Dr. Cooper.

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: Let's go, baby, we're losing daylight.

speaker: Sheldon
text: As you know, several weeks ago in our first encounter... We may have gotten off on the wrong foot... When I called you an idiot. And I just wanted to say that I was wrong... To point it out.

speaker: unknown
text: I'm sorry, we haven't been introduced.

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: - Dr. Eric gablehauser. - Mary Cooper, Sheldon's mom.

speaker: Gablehouser
text: Now, that's impossible. You must've had him when you were a teenager.

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: Oh, aren't you sweet. His father's dead.

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: - Recently? - Long enough.

speaker: unknown
text: Please. Sheldon, shouldn't you be working?

speaker: unknown
text: Okay.

speaker: Leonard
text: Hey, how did it go?

speaker: Sheldon
text: I got my job back.

speaker: Leonard
text: Really? What happened?

speaker: Sheldon
text: I'm not quite sure. It involves a part of the human experience that has always eluded me.

speaker: Leonard
text: Well, that narrows it down.

speaker: Mrs Cooper
text: I'm very proud of you, honey. You showed a lot of courage today.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Thanks, mom.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Is Dr. Gablehauser going to be my new daddy?

text: We'll see. Sleep tight.
